transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-11
Start: 16:00 EDT
Duration: 47 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Grace Liu (Redwood AE), Marco Ortega (Redwood SE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Alex Navarro (Holloway), Sana Patel (Holloway), Tom Reeves (Holloway FinOps)

Auto-summary (auto gen):
- Walkthrough of Console: per-route dashboards, usage attribution, cost breakdowns and export options
- Customer asks: route-level chargeback, SSO + SCIM provisioning, data residency for EU traffic, pilot with representative traffic for 1 week
- Next steps: pricing + security docs, sandbox project, benchmark runbook

Transcript:
[00:00] Grace: alright everyone hi thanks for joining, I'm Grace from Redwood inference, I'm the AE on this account, with Marco and Devon from our solutions team. how are you all?
[00:11] Alex: hey hi, doing well thanks. running a bit late this morning but good to be here.
[00:18] Sana: yep thanks - excited to see the console stuff, our finance team really wants per-route billing.
[00:25] Tom: yes, cut to the chase, how do we get cost per route so we can charge teams back?
[00:30] Grace: absolutely we'll show that - Marco do you want to drive the console demo?
[00:35] Marco: sure, I'll share my screen, give me a sec to pull up the Holloway sandbox demo tenant.
[00:44] 
[01:05] Marco: ok first page is the overall usage lens, you'll see token volume trends, tail latency percentiles and the big headline is route-level split on the right. there's a filter for time and region, and the routes are grouped by product line - note the labeling is driven by the route metadata that you send in the requests.
[01:30] Alex: quick q - we have about 120 routes but 75% of traffic is from 12 routes, can we collapse groups?
[01:39] Marco: yeah you can collapse and create route buckets, or define tags in the SDK so console groups them into cost-centers. We'll show a demo of that.
[01:48] 
[02:12] Marco: moving into a single-route view - here's route /chat/assist, top shows tokens/day, below is latency histogram, and on the right is cost attribution. cost is estimated from per-token execution cost + a compute amortization. that's configurable per deployment (hosted vs dedicated).
[02:31] Tom: amortization? like reserved GPU cost allocation?
[02:34] Marco: exactly - for Dedicated customers we let you input committed capacity and show the amortized cost per token. for hosted we use published unit pricing but you can override.
[02:45] Sana: do you support per-region pricing? we have EU data residency and different instance costs.
[02:50] Marco: yes - region-level cost factors can be toggled and we have a data residency tag so you can split EU vs US traffic.
[02:59] 
[03:20] Devon: also worth calling out the cache and batching column - if you enable prefix caching and batching the console simulates cost delta and shows expected throughput improvements. it's not perfect but gives a projection.
[03:35] Alex: hmm that's helpful. can that projection be exported? our finance team wants CSVs to push into our chargeback system.
[03:42] Marco: csv export is built-in, and we also have an API to pull per-route metrics on a schedule.
[03:49] 
[04:10] Tom: security quick q - we need SSO via SAML, RBAC and audit logs for token-level access. is that all in the console?
[04:18] Grace: yes, we support enterprise SSO (SAML + SCIM), role-based roles, and full audit logs for requests and config changes. we'll attach our SOC2 and ISO docs.
[04:30] Sana: and KMS? we can't have keys stored in your control plane for the private deployment.
[04:35] Marco: for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and you can bring your own keys, key material never leaves your VPC if you choose on-prem.
[04:44] 
[05:05] Alex: for the pilot we want representative traffic - 3 routes, 2M tokens/day total. can Redwood run that in a sandbox?
[05:12] Marco: yes, we can provision a sandbox project and pre-provision a dedicated pool for the pilot. recommended window is 7 days to get stable latency and cost numbers.
[05:22] Tom: and pricing for that pilot? high level is fine for now.
[05:26] Grace: we'll send tailored pricing for a short pilot and estimate cost per-token for the routes you share.
[05:33] 
[06:00] Marco: ok demo pivot - here's the cost-breakdown tab. you can select multiple routes and it shows total token cost, inferred infra overhead, cache savings and an annotation area where you manually add chargeback tags. also shows per-route p50/p95 latency before and after optimizations.
[06:22] Alex: annotation area - so ops can mark a route as experimental and costs won't be charged to production?
[06:28] Marco: correct, tags support billing exclusion or reallocation to a different cost center.
[06:35] 
[06:55] Devon: tiny callout - our Optimize toolkit suggests quantization profiles and batching thresholds per route. you can run the optimizer and it will produce a change-list you can test in a canary.
[07:07] Sana: do you have an eval harness? we need to ensure quality doesn't drop after quantization.
[07:11] Marco: yes, we have an evaluation harness with prompt sets, and you can tie alerts to regressions on a prompt set. we'll show a sample later if there's time.
[07:20] 
[08:05] Alex: about observability - what's the retention on token-level traces? we need 90 days for audits.
[08:12] Grace: retention is configurable for enterprise plans, 90 days is supported as an add-on.
[08:17] Tom: is there a hard cap on retention for hosted?
[08:21] Marco: for hosted there's usually tiered storage; for Private you control retention. we'll put specifics in the security doc.
[08:30] 
[09:00] Alex: inevitable question - why not just use ModelServeX internally? they have cheaper per-token on the benchmark we saw.
[09:07] Grace: good question - two points: 1) our console unifies hosted/dedicated/private operations so you don't rebuild tooling; 2) we provide explicit cost controls (batching, cache) and the amortization engine to plan reserved capacity, so TCO often ends up lower for production loads.
[09:28] Tom: also reliability matters, can you define SLOs?
[09:32] Marco: we have SLOs with Dedicated and fallbacks - automatic routing to warm-standby variants if capacity is constrained.
[09:40] 
[10:10] Marco: quick walkthrough of route tagging - here's a route label config, you can attach owner, cost-center, sensitivity, and a retention policy per route. those feed into the console dashboards automatically.
[10:28] Alex: perfect, that will let FinOps tie invoices to teams.
[10:32] Tom: one more on billing export - do you map tokens to invoice line items?
[10:36] Marco: yes, export includes SKU mapping and line-item cost if you use our billing integration. we create a mapping CSV that Finance imports.
[10:45] 
[11:10] Grace: small note on pilot success criteria - what would success look like for Holloway?
[11:16] Sana: two things: 1) <10% delta in quality from quantized model, 2) predictable cost per 1M tokens and ability to show chargeback to teams.
[11:26] Alex: and perf targets - p95 < 300ms for most interactive routes.
[11:31] Grace: great, we'll include those as acceptance criteria in the pilot runbook.
[11:36] 
[12:00] Marco: demo - routing policies screen. you can tier routes by latency sensitivity and cost-sensitivity. policy engine can route to cheaper model variant when not latency critical.
[12:17] Tom: that auto-fallback capability is exactly what we need for batch jobs.
[12:20] Marco: yep, and console shows fallback events and success rates.
[12:25] 
[12:50] Alex: how does KV cache and prefix caching factor into cost calc?
[12:56] Marco: console estimates cache hit rates based on your historical distribution; we show delta between cache-on and cache-off scenarios in cost previews.
[13:10] Sana: any limitations for air-gapped on-prem? we have a client in EU with heavy regulatory constraints.
[13:17] Marco: for air-gapped we ship an on-prem package and the control plane runs in a customer VPC, KMS integration for keys. there are some feature parity gaps but core metrics and console exports are supported. we'll share the matrix.
[13:30] 
[14:05] Grace: ok nearing the end, let's recap next steps. I'll send pricing and commercial terms for the pilot, Marco will provision a sandbox and share the pilot runbook, Alex will share the route list and traffic patterns.
[14:20] Alex: I'll get that by EOD tomorrow.
[14:23] Tom: one ask - can you share an example invoice mapping export so FinOps can review?
[14:27] Grace: yes we'll attach a sample CSV.
[14:30] Sana: and security docs please.
[14:33] Grace: we'll include SOC2, ISO and the KMS integration notes.
[14:36] 
[14:50] Marco: any other risks? I heard 'ModelServeX' mentioned; if you want we'll run a short bench to show throughput/cost delta on your real traffic.
[14:58] Alex: yes would like that, 1-week bench sounds fine.
[15:03] Grace: perfect we'll follow up with a concrete timeline. thanks everyone, we'll send the notes and items.
[15:12] Sana: thanks all, talk soon.
[15:15] end of recording
